docs.title: antcrew
docs.text: antcrew is an AI agent orchestration platform built for teams that need reliable, auditable, human-in-the-loop AI workflows.

docs.title: Products
docs.text: - **Platform** — web UI and API for managing workspaces, runs, tickets, and reviews - **Engine** — typed Python SDK for defining and executing agent contracts - **Proxy** — OpenAI-compatible proxy with provider routing and BYOK support

docs.title: Architecture at a glance
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Your code] -->|antcrew-engine SDK| B[antcrew-proxy]
    B -->|routes to| C[OpenAI / Anthropic / Groq / …]
    A -->|POST /runs| D[antcrew-platform API]
    D -->|TraceLog + Replay| E[(PostgreSQL)]
    D -->|HITL review| F[Human reviewer]

docs.title: Run lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> pending: POST /runs
    pending --> running: worker picks up
    running --> waiting_hitl: hitl_checkpoint reached
    waiting_hitl --> running: review approved
    waiting_hitl --> failed: review rejected
    running --> completed: all steps done
    running --> failed: unhandled exception
    completed --> [*]
    failed --> [*]

docs.title: Event streaming
docs.text: Events are written to PostgreSQL and broadcast to connected WebSocket clients in real time. The dashboard subscribes to /ws/runs/{run_id} to receive live updates without polling.

docs.title: Ticket creation
docs.text:
When a run completes, upsert_tickets_from_run() scans the run's events for any structured output that matches a ticket schema. Each ticket gets a workspace-scoped display ID (PREFIX-NNNNN) via an atomic counter:

UPDATE workspace
SET ticket_counter = ticket_counter + 1
WHERE id = :workspace_id
RETURNING ticket_prefix, ticket_counter;

docs.title: API key model
docs.text:
• Each workspace has one or more workspace API keys — these are the credentials your application uses
  • LLM provider keys are stored encrypted per-workspace (BYOK) and only decrypted at proxy request time
  • Platform uses short-lived session tokens for browser authentication

docs.title: HITL as a security gate
docs.text: Human-in-the-loop reviews prevent unreviewed AI outputs from reaching production systems. Any run can be configured to require approval before its output is acted on.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text: Every review decision (approve/reject), every run state change, and every settings modification is written to an append-only audit log with actor, timestamp, and diff.

docs.title: Engine — overview
docs.text:
antcrew-engine is the Python SDK for defining and running agent pipelines. It provides typed contracts, a TraceLog for full replay, and integrations with every major LLM provider.

pip install antcrew-engine

docs.title: Hello world
docs.text:
from antcrew import Agent, contract

@contract
def summarise(content: str) -> str:
    """Summarise the given text in one paragraph."""
    ...

agent = Agent(model="openai:gpt-4o-mini")
result = agent.run(summarise, content="Long document here…")
print(result)

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Typed contracts — Python functions as LLM prompts with type-checked inputs/outputs
  • TraceLog — every token, tool call, and decision is logged for replay
  • Provider-agnostic — swap models with one string change
  • HITL hooks — pause execution for human review at any step

docs.title: Typed contracts
docs.text: A contract is a Python function decorated with @contract. The function signature defines the LLM's input schema and expected output type. antcrew-engine enforces both at runtime.

docs.title: Basic contract
docs.text:
from antcrew import contract
from pydantic import BaseModel

class SummaryResult(BaseModel):
    title: str
    summary: str
    key_points: list[str]

@contract
def summarise_document(content: str, max_points: int = 5) -> SummaryResult:
    """
    Summarise the document and extract the most important points.
    Return no more than {max_points} key points.
    """
    ...

docs.title: Chaining contracts
docs.text:
@contract
def translate(text: str, target_language: str) -> str:
    """Translate the text to {target_language}."""
    ...

# Chain: summarise → translate
agent = Agent(model="openai:gpt-4o")
summary = agent.run(summarise_document, content=doc)
translated = agent.run(translate, text=summary.summary, target_language="Spanish")

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: If the LLM returns a response that doesn't match the output schema, antcrew-engine retries automatically (up to max_retries attempts) before raising ContractValidationError.

docs.title: Custom agents
docs.text: Beyond simple contract calls, antcrew-engine lets you define multi-step agents with tools, memory, and conditional branching.

docs.title: Agent with tools
docs.text:
from antcrew import Agent, tool, contract

@tool
def search_web(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web and return the top result."""
    # your implementation
    ...

@tool
def read_file(path: str) -> str:
    """Read a file from disk."""
    with open(path) as f:
        return f.read()

@contract
def research_topic(topic: str) -> str:
    """Research {topic} using available tools and write a concise report."""
    ...

agent = Agent(
    model="openai:gpt-4o",
    tools=[search_web, read_file],
)
report = agent.run(research_topic, topic="quantum computing trends 2025")

docs.title: HITL pause points
docs.text:
from antcrew import Agent, hitl_checkpoint

agent = Agent(model="anthropic:claude-sonnet-5")

draft = agent.run(write_draft, topic="...")

# Pause here and wait for a human to approve before continuing
approved_draft = hitl_checkpoint(
    value=draft,
    prompt="Please review this draft before it is sent.",
    platform_api_key="...",
)

agent.run(send_email, content=approved_draft)

The HITL checkpoint creates a review in the platform dashboard and blocks execution until approved or rejected.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: antcrew-engine supports every major LLM provider through a single string prefix.

docs.title: Supported prefixes
docs.text: Prefix Provider Example model openai: OpenAI openai:gpt-4o anthropic: Anthropic anthropic:claude-sonnet-5 groq: Groq groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile gemini: Google Gemini gemini:gemini-2.0-flash moonshot: Moonshot AI moonshot:moonshot-v1-8k simulated: Built-in mock simulated:echo

docs.title: Switching providers
docs.text:
# GPT-4o
agent = Agent(model="openai:gpt-4o")

# Claude — same code, different model string
agent = Agent(model="anthropic:claude-sonnet-5")

# Free local mock for tests
agent = Agent(model="simulated:echo")

docs.title: BYOK via the Proxy
docs.text:
When using antcrew-proxy, your keys are stored in the platform and injected at request time. Your application code never handles credentials directly:

agent = Agent(
    model="openai:gpt-4o",
    base_url="https://proxy.antcrew.org",  # proxy handles the key
)

docs.title: TraceLog & Replay
docs.text: Every run executed by antcrew-engine produces a TraceLog — a structured, append-only log of every LLM call, tool invocation, and intermediate result.

docs.title: What gets logged
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Agent.run called] --> B[TraceLog: run_start]
    B --> C[LLM request]
    C --> D[TraceLog: llm_request + tokens]
    D --> E{Tool call?}
    E -->|yes| F[TraceLog: tool_call + result]
    F --> C
    E -->|no| G[Parse output]
    G --> H{Valid?}
    H -->|no| I[TraceLog: validation_error]
    I --> C
    H -->|yes| J[TraceLog: run_complete]

docs.title: Replay
docs.text:
Any past run can be replayed exactly from its TraceLog without making new LLM calls:

from antcrew import replay_run

# Replay a past run from its ID
result = replay_run("run_01HXYZ...")

Useful for:

  • Debugging — step through exactly what the agent did
  • Testing — assert on deterministic outputs without API costs
  • Audit — demonstrate to stakeholders what the model decided and why

docs.title: Shipping logs to the Platform
docs.text:
from antcrew import Agent
from antcrew.platform import PlatformSink

agent = Agent(
    model="openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    trace_sink=PlatformSink(
        base_url="https://platform-int.antcrew.org",
        api_key="your-key",
    ),
)

All events are streamed to the platform in real time and visible in the Runs dashboard.

docs.title: Platform — overview
docs.text: antcrew-platform is the web application and REST API that ties everything together: workspaces, runs, tickets, HITL reviews, evals, and webhooks.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text: Concept Description Workspace Isolated tenant with its own API keys, members, and settings Run A single execution of an agent pipeline — has events, tickets, and a TraceLog Ticket An action item generated by a run, with a display ID (PREFIX-00001) HITL Review A human approval gate attached to a run or ticket Eval Automated quality check run on a schedule or on demand Webhook Outbound event notification to your own endpoint

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant SDK as antcrew-engine
    participant API as Platform API
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant Human

    SDK->>API: POST /runs (pipeline_def + input)
    API->>DB: persist run + events
    API-->>SDK: run_id
    SDK->>API: POST /runs/{id}/events (TraceLog)
    API->>DB: append events
    API->>Human: notify (webhook / email)
    Human->>API: POST /reviews/{id}/approve
    API-->>SDK: resume signal

docs.text: Environment URL Trigger INT platform-int.antcrew.org Auto on every push to main UAT platform-uat.antcrew.org Manual dispatch → Deploy → uat PROD (coming soon) Manual dispatch → Deploy → prod, requires UAT gate

docs.title: Deploying to UAT
docs.text:
1. Go to GitHub → Actions → Deploy
  2. Click Run workflow
  3. Set environment to uat, choose the auto-shutdown window (1–8h)
  4. The server is created from a snapshot, the app is deployed, and the server self-deletes after the window

docs.title: Restarting UAT without redeploying
docs.text:
If the UAT server shut down and you want to test against the same build:

  1. GitHub → Actions → UAT — on-demand start
  2. Run workflow → choose hours

This restarts the existing server and resets the auto-delete timer.

docs.title: INT → PROD promotion
docs.text: Prod deploys require the last UAT deployment to be successful (enforced by the gate-prod job in the Deploy workflow). This prevents unvalidated code from reaching production.

docs.title: Evals
docs.text: Evals are automated quality checks that run your agent pipelines against a fixed dataset and score the outputs.

docs.title: Creating an eval
docs.text:
1. Go to Evals in the dashboard
  2. Click New eval
  3. Select a pipeline definition and a dataset
  4. Configure scoring criteria (exact match, LLM-as-judge, custom function)

docs.title: Scheduling
docs.text: Evals can run: - On demand — triggered manually or via API - On schedule — cron-based (e.g. daily at 02:00 UTC) - On deploy — automatically after each successful INT deploy

docs.title: Compare runs
docs.text: The Compare view lets you run the same dataset through two different configurations (different models, prompts, or pipeline versions) side by side to measure regressions or improvements.

docs.title: 1. Create a workspace
docs.text: After logging in, create a workspace. Each workspace has its own API key, members, and LLM provider settings.

docs.title: 2. Add an LLM provider key
docs.text: Go to Settings → Providers and add your API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, or any other supported provider. These are stored encrypted (BYOK — bring your own key).

docs.title: 3. Submit your first run
docs.text:
import httpx

client = httpx.Client(base_url="https://platform-int.antcrew.org")

response = client.post("/api/runs", json={
    "pipeline_def": "my-pipeline",
    "input": {"prompt": "summarise this document", "content": "..."},
}, headers={"X-API-Key": "your-workspace-api-key"})

run_id = response.json()["id"]
print(f"Run started: {run_id}")

docs.title: 4. Monitor in the dashboard
docs.text: Open /runs to see the run status, events, and generated tickets in real time.

docs.title: HITL Reviews
docs.text: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) reviews let a human approve, reject, or modify AI output before it has downstream effects.

docs.title: Creating a review
docs.text: Reviews are created automatically when a run hits a hitl_checkpoint, or manually from the dashboard.

docs.title: Review workflow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Run
    participant Platform
    participant Reviewer

    Run->>Platform: POST /reviews (pending)
    Platform->>Reviewer: notify (webhook / email)
    Reviewer->>Platform: GET /reviews (see queue)
    Reviewer->>Platform: POST /reviews/{id}/approve
    Platform->>Run: resume signal
    Run->>Run: continue execution

docs.title: Assignees
docs.text: Reviews can be assigned to specific workspace members. Unassigned reviews are visible to all members with the reviewer role.

docs.title: Audit trail
docs.text: Every review action (assign, approve, reject, comment) is recorded in the audit log with the reviewer's identity and timestamp.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text: A run is the top-level unit of work. It maps to one execution of an agent pipeline.

docs.title: Create a run
docs.text:
POST /api/runs
X-API-Key: your-key

{
  "pipeline_def": "summarise-and-file",
  "input": { "document_id": "doc_123" },
  "template_id": "optional-template-id"
}

Response includes id, status, and a WebSocket URL for live updates.

docs.title: Run statuses
docs.text: Status Meaning pending Queued, not yet started running Actively executing waiting_hitl Paused at a HITL checkpoint completed Finished successfully failed Ended with an error

docs.title: Tickets
docs.text: Tickets are structured action items extracted from run output.

docs.title: Display IDs
docs.text:
Each workspace has a configurable prefix (e.g. PROJ). Tickets get sequential IDs: PROJ-00001, PROJ-00002, etc.

Configure the prefix in Settings → Ticket Settings.

docs.title: Linking to GitHub
docs.text: If a workspace has a GitHub repo configured, the ticket detail view shows linked commits and PRs that contain the ticket display ID in their message.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: Webhooks deliver real-time event notifications to your own endpoint when things happen in antcrew.

docs.title: Supported events
docs.text: Event Trigger run.created A new run is submitted run.completed A run finishes successfully run.failed A run ends with an error ticket.created A ticket is extracted from a run review.created A HITL review is opened review.resolved A review is approved or rejected

docs.title: Configuring a webhook
docs.text: Go to Webhooks in the dashboard and click Add webhook. Provide: - URL — your HTTPS endpoint - Events — which events to subscribe to - Secret — used to verify the signature on incoming requests

docs.title: Verifying signatures
docs.text:
Each request includes an X-Antcrew-Signature header. Verify it with HMAC-SHA256:

import hmac, hashlib

def verify(payload: bytes, signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text: A workspace is an isolated tenant. Everything — runs, tickets, reviews, provider keys — belongs to a workspace.

docs.title: Members & roles
docs.text: Role Capabilities owner Full access including billing and member management admin All workspace settings, no billing member Create runs, view tickets, submit reviews reviewer View and action HITL reviews only

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text:
Each workspace has one or more API keys. Use them in the X-API-Key header for all API requests and in the antcrew-engine SDK.

agent = Agent(
    model="openai:gpt-4o",
    platform_api_key="acw_live_...",
)

Keys can be rotated at any time from Settings → API Keys without downtime.

docs.title: Provider keys (BYOK)
docs.text: Add your own LLM provider API keys in Settings → Providers. Keys are encrypted at rest. The proxy uses them to make calls on your behalf — your application code never sees them.

docs.title: Proxy — overview
docs.text: antcrew-proxy is an OpenAI-compatible HTTP proxy that sits between your application and LLM providers. It handles key injection, request logging, cost tracking, and provider routing.

docs.title: Why use the proxy?
docs.text:
• BYOK without touching keys in code — keys live in the platform, not in your app
  • Drop-in replacement — change base_url only, no other code changes
  • Provider routing — route openai:* to OpenAI, anthropic:* to Anthropic, etc.
  • Observability — every request is logged with tokens, cost, and latency

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import openai

client = openai.OpenAI(
    base_url="https://proxy.antcrew.org/v1",
    api_key="your-antcrew-workspace-key",  # platform key, not OpenAI key
)

# Works exactly like the OpenAI SDK
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Required Description PLATFORM_URL yes URL of antcrew-platform API PLATFORM_INTERNAL_KEY yes Service-to-service key for key lookup PORT no Port to listen on (default: 8080) LOG_FORMAT no json or text (default: json)

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
services:
  proxy:
    image: ghcr.io/iagop03/antcrew-proxy:latest
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      PLATFORM_URL: https://platform-int.antcrew.org
      PLATFORM_INTERNAL_KEY: ${INTERNAL_KEY}

docs.title: Supported ports (Cloudflare proxy-compatible)
docs.text: The proxy listens on port 8080 by default, which is in Cloudflare's list of supported HTTP ports, making it compatible with Cloudflare proxy without any additional configuration.

docs.title: Provider routing
docs.text: The proxy routes requests to the correct provider based on the model field prefix.

docs.title: How routing works
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Request: model=openai:gpt-4o] --> B{Parse prefix}
    B -->|openai:| C[Inject OpenAI key]
    B -->|anthropic:| D[Inject Anthropic key]
    B -->|groq:| E[Inject Groq key]
    C & D & E --> F[Forward to provider API]
    F --> G[Return response]

The proxy strips the prefix before forwarding so the provider receives the bare model name (gpt-4o, claude-sonnet-5, etc.).

docs.title: Fallback routing
docs.text: If a prefix is not recognised, the request is forwarded to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured as the default provider.

docs.title: Per-workspace keys
docs.text:
Each workspace can have different keys for each provider. The proxy resolves the correct key by workspace API key → workspace → provider key lookup.

Request: X-API-Key: ws_abc123, model: anthropic:claude-sonnet-5
  → look up workspace for ws_abc123
  → find workspace's Anthropic key
  → inject key + forward to api.anthropic.com
